incidents.summary: An employment tribunal found that Mears discriminated against a disabled former manager and victimised her through dismissal, ordering £964,465 in compensation while the company appealed parts of the ruling.

sources.title: Inside Housing - News - Social housing contractor ordered to pay former employee nearly £1m in disability discrimination case
sources.quote: The ruling found both that there was a failure to give Ms Austin the opportunity to apply for a new role at the repairs contractor and that her subsequent dismissal amounted to disability discrimination.

sources.title: Inside Housing - News - Social housing contractor ordered to pay former employee nearly £1m in disability discrimination case
sources.quote: The company has been ordered to pay Ms Austin £964,465 in total.

sources.title: Inside Housing - News - Social housing contractor ordered to pay former employee nearly £1m in disability discrimination case
sources.quote: According to the judgment, Mears conceded that the dismissal was “unfair”. However, the firm is appealing parts of the ruling.

incidents.summary: Mears Scotland LLP was accused of falsifying at least 13,000 maintenance records, and councillors postponed signing a new £1.8 billion contract with the firm.

sources.title: Scottish Labour transparency row over Hamilton by-election candidate | The National
sources.quote: Last year it was alleged that Mears Scotland LLP had falsified at least 13,000 maintenance records, after a whistleblower reported the firm to the local authority’s auditors.

sources.title: Scottish Labour transparency row over Hamilton by-election candidate | The National
sources.quote: North Lanarkshire councillors then postponed signing a new £1.8 billion contract with the firm, that would have provided maintenance and repairs for the authority’s 36,700 council houses and every council building.

incidents.summary: Council inspections identified mould, loose wiring and missing smoke alarms at Mears asylum accommodation in Gateshead, while Glasgow reported a cockroach infestation requiring a treatment plan.

sources.title: Rodents, mould and cockroaches: The asylum homes costing taxpayers £1bn
sources.quote: In Gateshead, housing inspectors discovered Mears’ properties had issues including mould, loose wiring and a lack of smoke alarms.

sources.title: Rodents, mould and cockroaches: The asylum homes costing taxpayers £1bn
sources.quote: In Glasgow, the council reported an “infestation of cockroaches” in one property for which Mears had to come up with a treatment plan.

incidents.summary: A Glasgow support charity accused Mears of routinely failing to provide the required five days’ notice before moving asylum seekers, causing unnecessary stress and suffering.

sources.title: Housing company accused of ‘re-traumatising’ asylum seekers
sources.quote: Mears Group – which will be paid £1.1bn by the Home Office over ten years to provide asylum accommodation – is contractually obliged to provide five days’ notice before moving people.

sources.title: Housing company accused of ‘re-traumatising’ asylum seekers
sources.quote: But the Asylum Seeker Housing project, a support service run by Glasgow charity Community Infosource, says it is routinely failing to do this, leading to unnecessary stress and suffering.

sources.title: Housing company accused of ‘re-traumatising’ asylum seekers
sources.quote: At least one was given just ten minutes’ notice, causing panic and anxiety.
